title: 7 Website Mistakes That Cost Medical Practices Patients
desc: Slow pages, hidden phone numbers and other common errors, and how to fix each one.
text:
Your website is your front door. If it is slow, confusing or hard to use, patients walk away without telling you. The good news is that most problems are easy to fix. Here are seven common mistakes and what to do about each one.

## 1. A slow website
If a page takes more than three seconds to load, a large share of visitors leave. Slow sites also rank lower on Google. The usual causes are huge photos, too many plug ins and cheap hosting.

To fix it, compress your images, remove tools you do not use, and move to fast hosting. Then test your speed with Google PageSpeed Insights and fix the biggest warnings first.

## 2. A site that is not made for phones
More than half of your visitors are on a phone. If the text is tiny, the buttons are too close together or the menu is hard to open, they will leave. Open your site on your own phone and try to book a visit. If it feels hard to you, it is harder for a patient who is in pain or in a hurry.

## 3. Hidden contact details
A patient who is ready to call should find the number in three seconds. Put your phone number and a "Book now" button at the top of every page, and repeat them at the bottom. Add your address and a map on the contact page. Every extra click costs you calls.

## 4. Too much medical language
Doctors are used to medical terms, but patients are not. Pages full of long words feel cold and confusing. Write the way you speak to a patient in the room. Use short sentences, explain any medical term, and say what the next step is.

## 5. Only stock photos, or old photos
Patients want to know who will treat them. Real photos of your doctors, your team and your office build trust faster than any slogan. Use a professional photo shoot, keep the images fresh, and add a short bio with a friendly face for each provider.

## 6. No proof that you are good
Anyone can say they are the best. Proof is what convinces. Show your star rating, patient reviews, board certifications, awards, years of experience and the hospitals you work with. Where the rules allow, add before and after results or patient stories. Place proof near your main buttons so it supports the decision.

## 7. One page for every service
A single services page cannot rank for every treatment. Give each service its own page with a clear title, a plain explanation, answers to common questions, and a call to action. This helps patients find the right page from Google, and it helps Google understand what you treat.

## A five minute check
Open your site on your phone right now. Can you find the phone number in three seconds? Does the page load fast? Is it clear what you treat and how to book? If any answer is no, start with that one.
